column2: We put out something that describes our new approach to handle the patch gap: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/privacy-security/defendi...

There are some heavy limitations worth highlighting here.

Firefox compromises also depended on a separate, previously unpublished vulnerability. Mozilla patched that vulnerability in Firefox 159.0 on October 27, 2026.

The researchers were unable to reproduce comparable results against Chrome, despite spending roughly $100,000 testing it.
What is the solution implied here? Attackers - whoever they are - already have them, so perhaps it's time we close the patch gap instead.

The article doesn't establish whether AI ultimately benefits attackers more than defenders. Open weight models give defenders access to the same capabilities. At the very least the community has a level of symmetry they wouldn't otherwise have.
